# Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq.md

`DataVoTable<T>` lets you query `[DataVoTable]` models with C# lambdas that Roslyn compiles into prepared queries and zero-allocation storage scans at build time. No expression trees are constructed and no reflection runs at runtime, making compiled LINQ safe for Native AOT and 60/120 FPS game loops.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE game; USE game;");
db.EnsurePlayerTable();

DataVoTable<Player> players = db.Table<Player>();

// Pass values as state with a static lambda: zero closure allocation
Player? top = players.FirstOrDefault(1, static (p, id) => p.Id == id);
List<Player> leaderboard = players
    .Where(500, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(10)
    .ToList();
```

::: info DataVo Extension
Compile-time LINQ interceptors, in-storage zero-allocation aggregates, and 3D spatial index queries (`WithinRadius`, `WithinBoundingBox`, `NearestNeighbors`) are `.NET`-native DataVo extensions powered by `DataVo.Generators`.
:::

## Enabling Interceptors

Installing the `DataVo.Generators` NuGet package enables C# 12 interceptors automatically. If you reference the generator via a project reference, add the generated namespace to your `.csproj`:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <InterceptorsNamespaces>$(InterceptorsNamespaces);DataVo.Generated</InterceptorsNamespaces>
</PropertyGroup>
```

On compilers without interceptors (such as Unity), the same code compiles and returns identical results via fallback scans; use generated `Get<Model>ById` methods or prepared statements on hot paths.

## Supported LINQ Operators

| Operator | Compiled Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Where` | Translates `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `&&`, `\|\|`, boolean flags, and `null` checks. Uses PK/B-Tree indexes when available; streams in 1,024-row pages otherwise. |
| `FirstOrDefault`, `SingleOrDefault` | PK equality on `Lsm` reads a single row (0 B on miss). |
| `Count`, `Any`, `Sum`, `Min`, `Max` | Compiles directly into the storage scan (or `[Columnar]` index) for numeric/bool/date/Guid columns (**0 B allocated** once warm). |
| `OrderBy`, `OrderByDescending`, `ThenBy`, `ThenByDescending` | Emits `ORDER BY`; combined with `Take`, retains only top-K rows during the scan. `string` keys order ordinally (as SQL `ORDER BY` does), not by the current culture; pass a comparer (`OrderBy(p => p.Name, comparer)`) to order in memory instead. |
| `Skip`, `Take` | Emits `OFFSET @offset LIMIT @limit` following `Enumerable` clamping semantics. |
| `Select` | Projects only the referenced columns (`SELECT name, score ...`) without instantiating full models. |
| `ExecuteDelete`, `ExecuteUpdate` | Emits single atomic `DELETE` or `UPDATE` statements (`Set`, `SetNull`, and `+`, `-`, `*` column arithmetic). |

### Zero-Allocation Aggregates & Bulk Updates

```csharp
// 0 B allocated on warm InMemory and Lsm tables (accelerated further if Score is [Columnar])
int elites = players.Where(1000, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min).Count();
long totalScore = players.Where(1000, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min).Sum(static p => p.Score);

// Atomic server-side bulk update
int boosted = players
    .Where(500, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .ExecuteUpdate(100, static (set, bonus) => set.Set(p => p.Score, p => p.Score + bonus));
```

### Build Diagnostics

Queries that cannot be compiled still return accurate results via an in-memory fallback (except `ExecuteUpdate`, which has no fallback) and emit a build diagnostic:

| Code | Severity | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATAVOL001` | Warning | Lambda captures a local or instance member; pass it as state with a `static` lambda. |
| `DATAVOL002` | Warning | Predicate uses an unsupported construct (method call, arithmetic, or cross-column comparison). |
| `DATAVOL003` | Warning | `InterceptorsNamespaces` does not include `DataVo.Generated`. |
| `DATAVOL004` | Warning | `OrderBy`/`ThenBy` key or `Select` projection falls back to in-memory execution. |
| `DATAVOL005` | Error | `ExecuteUpdate` cannot be compiled (captured variable, PK assignment, or unsupported expression). |

## 3D Spatial Queries

Any `System.Numerics.Vector3` property on a `[DataVoTable]` model is stored as `VECTOR(3)` and can be queried spatially:

```csharp
using System.Numerics;

var origin = new Vector3(0f, 0f, 0f);

// Stream players inside a 50-unit sphere (surface inclusive)
foreach (Player p in players.WithinRadius(origin, radius: 50f)) { }

// Stream players inside an axis-aligned bounding box
List<Player> inZone = players.WithinBoundingBox(new(-10, -10, -10), new(10, 10, 10)).ToList();

// 5 closest players (uses [SpatialIndex] Euclidean HNSW; pass exact: true for exact scan)
IReadOnlyList<Player> nearest = players.NearestNeighbors(origin, k: 5);
```

- `WithinRadius` and `WithinBoundingBox` test stored coordinates in double precision before allocating models, so non-matching rows allocate nothing.
- `NearestNeighbors` uses the `[SpatialIndex]` Euclidean HNSW index (`sx_<table>_<column>`) when present, or falls back to an exact streaming scan when `exact: true`, unindexed, or inside a transaction.
- When a model has multiple `Vector3` properties, pass `column: "PropertyName"`. Nullable `Vector3?` rows with `null` never match.

## Reactive Subscriptions

Composed `DataVoTable<T>` queries (`Where`, `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`, `Skip`, `Take`, `Select`) integrate directly with DataVo's Z-set incremental view engine:

- **`.Subscribe(Action<QueryChange<T>> onChanged)`** delivers strongly-typed `Added`, `Removed`, `Updated`, and `UpdatedBefore` deltas when `db.DispatchPendingNotifications()` drains committed writes.
- **`.SubscribeInto(Memory<T> destination, Action<int> onUpdated)`** writes the live window directly into a caller-owned buffer with **0 B** heap allocations per drain for compiled `.Select(...)` struct projections:

```csharp
public struct HudSlot { public int Id; public int Score; }

var hud = new HudSlot[3];
using var sub = players
    .Where(100, static (p, min) => p.Score >= min)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(3)
    .Select(static p => new HudSlot { Id = p.Id, Score = p.Score })
    .SubscribeInto(hud.AsMemory(), count => RenderHud(hud.AsSpan(0, count)));
```

## See Also

- [Roslyn Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators): `[DataVoTable]` annotations, generated helpers, and `[DataVoQuery]`
- [Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views): Pull-drain Z-set IVM model and choosing a subscription API
- [Compiled Scan Kernels](/manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels): How zero-allocation scan predicates and columnar indexes work

# Native AOT Deployment

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/native-aot
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/native-aot.md

`DataVo.Core`, `DataVo.Data`, and `DataVo.Generators` are built and tested for `.NET 10` Native AOT. Trim and AOT analyzers are enabled across the core and ADO.NET assemblies with `IL2026` and `IL3050` treated as build errors and verified on every change.

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
  <PublishAot>true</PublishAot>
  <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>
</PropertyGroup>
```

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-arm64
```

## Package AOT Compatibility

| Package / Feature | Native AOT Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVo.Core` | **Verified** | Runtime SQL parser/executor, LSM/InMemory storage, `StreamQuery`, `StreamRef`, `Subscribe`, and `SubscribeZeroAlloc` use zero reflection. |
| `DataVo.Data` | **Verified** | `DataVoConnection`, `DataVoCommand`, `DataVoDataReader`, and `DataVoTransaction` are trim- and AOT-clean. |
| `DataVo.Generators` | **Verified** | `[DataVoTable]`, `[DataVoQuery]`, compiled LINQ interceptors, and `.SubscribeInto()` emit static C# at build time. |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | **Excluded** | Depends on EF Core's runtime infrastructure and is not covered by the Native AOT guarantee. |

## Writing AOT-Safe DataVo Code

- **Use `DataVo.Generators` for typed queries:** Prefer `[DataVoTable]` compiled LINQ and `[DataVoQuery]` over reflection-based mappers.
- **Avoid reflection-based micro-ORMs unless AOT-enabled:** `DataVo.Data` itself is AOT-clean, but third-party libraries layered on top (such as unconfigured Dapper reflection paths) govern their own AOT compatibility.
- **Use zero-allocation streaming on hot paths:** `StreamRef()` and `SubscribeZeroAlloc()` operate on `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` and `RowRef` structs with zero reflection and zero managed heap allocations.
- **Keep `DataVoContext.Insert<T>` types preserved:** `Insert<T>` carries `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` annotations so the trimmer preserves public properties and parameterless constructors, or use source-generated `db.Insert(player)` for zero-reflection writes.

## Verification

The repository validates AOT cleanliness with `scripts/check-aot-baseline.sh`, which publishes an AOT smoke application exercising `DataVo.Core`, `DataVo.Data`, and `DataVo.Generators` under `PublishAot=true`.

## See Also

- [Roslyn Source Generators](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators): Compile-time helpers and `[DataVoQuery]`
- [Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq): Zero-reflection LINQ interceptors
- [Zero-Allocation Rows](/manual/internals/zero-allocation-rows): `RowRef` and `StreamRef` internals

---

# ADO.NET Provider (`DataVo.Data`)

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/ado-net
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/ado-net.md

`DataVo.Data` implements the standard `System.Data.Common` abstractions (`DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbDataReader`, `DbTransaction`, `DbParameter`) over the in-process DataVo engine. Any library targeting `IDbConnection`, including [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper), works without custom adapters.

```csharp
using DataVo.Data;

using var conn = new DataVoConnection("StorageMode=Lsm;DataSource=./game-data");
conn.Open();

using var cmd = conn.CreateCommand();
cmd.CommandText = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80), score INT)";
cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();

cmd.CommandText = "INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (@id, @name, @score)";
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", 1);
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", "Ada");
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@score", 1200);
cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();
```

## Connection Strings & Lifecycle

Use `DataVoConnectionStringBuilder` or a semicolon-delimited string with three supported keys:

| Key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StorageMode` | `InMemory` | `InMemory` or `Lsm`. Any other value throws `ArgumentException`. |
| `DataSource` | `"datavo"` | Database name (and storage directory path for `Lsm`). |

When `conn.Open()` runs, it initializes the embedded engine, executes `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` for the `DataSource` database name, and selects it with `USE`. `Close()` rolls back any uncommitted transaction and releases the session.

## Provider Types

| `System.Data.Common` Base | DataVo Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DbConnection` | `DataVoConnection` | In-process engine handle; no network socket or connection pool. |
| `DbCommand` | `DataVoCommand` | Text commands with `@param` placeholders and `Prepare()`. |
| `DbDataReader` | `DataVoDataReader` | Forward-only reader over materialized command results. |
| `DbTransaction` | `DataVoTransaction` | Supports `Commit()`, `Rollback()`, and savepoints (`Save`, `Rollback(name)`, `Release`). |
| `DbParameter` | `DataVoParameter` | Supports `Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", value)`. |
| `DbConnectionStringBuilder` | `DataVoConnectionStringBuilder` | Strongly-typed builder for `StorageMode` and `DataSource`. |
| `Exception` | `DataVoException` | Exposes `ErrorCode`, `Line`, and `Column`. |

`DataVo.Data` does **not** ship a `DbProviderFactory`.

## Transactions & Prepared Commands

```csharp
using var tx = conn.BeginTransaction();

using var update = conn.CreateCommand();
update.CommandText = "UPDATE players SET score = @score WHERE id = @id";
update.Parameters.AddWithValue("@score", 1500);
update.Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", 1);
update.Prepare();
update.ExecuteNonQuery();

tx.Save("checkpoint1");
tx.Rollback("checkpoint1");
tx.Commit();
```

Calling `Prepare()` (or using parameterized commands) routes execution through DataVo's prepared-statement cache so repeated executions skip SQL parsing.

## Behavior Notes

- **Materialized reader:** `ExecuteReader()` executes the statement and walks materialized rows; for zero-allocation streaming, use `DataVoContext.StreamRef()` or compiled LINQ.
- **Metadata before `Read()`:** `GetName` and `GetFieldType` are available before the first `Read()` call. Column types are inferred from the first non-null value (`object` if all values are null).
- **Synchronous async wrappers:** `ExecuteReaderAsync` and other async methods complete synchronously on the calling thread because storage is in-process.
- **Timeouts and cancellation:** `Cancel()` is a no-op and `CommandTimeout` does not abort running statements; lock waits are bounded by `LockAcquireTimeoutMs`.
- **Single-process directory ownership:** Multiple `DataVoConnection` instances in the same process share one engine for a given directory; a second process opening the same directory fails with `DV7001_DATABASE_IN_USE`.

## See Also

- [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper): Using Dapper over `DataVoConnection`
- [Error Handling](/manual/reference/error-handling): `DataVoException` and `DV*` error codes
- [Native AOT Deployment](/manual/client-interfaces/native-aot): Trim and AOT compatibility for `DataVo.Data`

---

# Dapper

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/dapper
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/dapper.md

Dapper works directly with DataVo via `DataVo.Data`. Because `DataVoConnection` implements `DbConnection`, Dapper's `IDbConnection` extension methods require no DataVo-specific adapter package.

```csharp
using Dapper;
using DataVo.Data;

using var conn = new DataVoConnection("StorageMode=InMemory;DataSource=game");
conn.Open();

conn.Execute("CREATE TABLE players (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80), score INT)");
conn.Execute(
    "INSERT INTO players (id, name, score) VALUES (@Id, @Name, @Score)",
    new { Id = 1, Name = "Ada", Score = 1200 });

List<Player> top = conn
    .Query<Player>("SELECT id, name, score FROM players WHERE score >= @min", new { min = 500 })
    .ToList();

int total = conn.ExecuteScalar<int>("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players");
```

Install both packages:

```bash
dotnet add package DataVo.Data --prerelease
dotnet add package Dapper
```

## Transactions & Parameterized Queries

Pass an `IDbTransaction` from `conn.BeginTransaction()` directly to Dapper's `Execute` and `Query` calls. Named parameters (`@Id`, `@min`) bind through `DataVoCommand`'s prepared-statement pipeline.

```csharp
using var tx = conn.BeginTransaction();

conn.Execute(
    "UPDATE players SET score = score + @bonus WHERE id = @id",
    new { bonus = 250, id = 1 },
    tx);

tx.Commit(); // or tx.Rollback()
```

### Verified Dapper Surface

Tested against `DataVoConnection` with Dapper `2.1.35`:

| Dapper Call | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Execute` with anonymous-object parameters | Returns exact rows-affected count. |
| `Query<T>` / `QuerySingleOrDefault<T>` | Maps columns to POCO properties by name. |
| `ExecuteScalar<T>` | Returns the first column of the first row. |
| `QueryAsync<T>` | Completes synchronously (in-process engine). |
| `Execute` with `IDbTransaction` | Full `Commit()` / `Rollback()` participation. |

Features outside this verified set (such as multi-mapping, `QueryMultiple`, or list parameter expansion) pass through standard ADO.NET; validate them against your schema before relying on them.

## Dapper vs. Compiled LINQ

| Aspect | Dapper | [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query style | Raw SQL strings | Compile-time-checked C# lambdas |
| Row mapping | Reflection-based (per Dapper) | Source-generated, zero reflection |
| Heap allocations | Per-row POCO + Dapper overhead | **0 B** warm aggregates & buffered views |
| Native AOT | Governed by Dapper AOT support | Full Native AOT support |
| Best fit | Joins, ad-hoc SQL, existing Dapper code | Hot-path lookups, filtered aggregates, game loops |

Both interfaces can share the same underlying database: use Dapper for flexible SQL and compiled LINQ for hot paths.

## See Also

- [ADO.NET Provider (DataVo.Data)](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net): Connection strings, savepoints, and reader behavior
- [Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq): Zero-reflection compile-time queries
- [Choosing an Interface](/manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface): Compare all DataVo client APIs

# Entity Framework Core

> Source route: /manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework
> Source file: manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework.md

::: warning Experimental Preview: Excluded from Native AOT
`DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` is an **experimental integration bridge**, not a standalone migration-capable EF Core provider. It relies on a host EF provider (such as `UseInMemoryDatabase`) for EF infrastructure services and is **excluded from DataVo's Native AOT guarantee**. For production or AOT workloads, use [`DataVoContext`](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api), [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq), or [ADO.NET / Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net).
:::

`DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` lets EF Core users evaluate DataVo-backed persistence and DataVo-native queries while keeping familiar `DbContext` and `DbSet<T>` models.

```csharp
using DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<GameDbContext>()
    .UseInMemoryDatabase("datavo-ef-host")
    .UseDataVo(dataVo => dataVo
        .UseInMemoryStorage()
        .WithDataSource("game"))
    .Options;

using var ctx = new GameDbContext(options);
ctx.EnsureDataVoCreated();

ctx.Players.Add(new Player { Id = 1, Name = "Ada", Score = 1200, Region = "EU" });
ctx.SaveChanges();

List<Player> top = ctx.QueryFromDataVo<Player>(q => q
    .Where(static p => p.Score >= 1000)
    .OrderByDescending(static p => p.Score)
    .Take(10));
```

## Configuring `DataVoDbContext`

Derive from `DataVoDbContext` to access `LoadFromDataVo`, `QueryFromDataVo`, `QueryFromDataVoAsync`, and `ExplainQueryFromDataVo`:

```csharp
public sealed class GameDbContext : DataVoDbContext
{
    public GameDbContext(DbContextOptions<GameDbContext> options) : base(options) { }

    public DbSet<Player> Players => Set<Player>();

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        modelBuilder.Entity<Player>(entity =>
        {
            entity.ToTable("players");
            entity.HasKey(static p => p.Id);
            entity.Property(static p => p.Name).HasMaxLength(80);
        });
    }
}
```

- **`UseDataVo(...)`** attaches DataVo storage options (or a DataVo connection string) to `DbContextOptionsBuilder`.
- **`EnsureDataVoCreated()`** initializes the mapped tables in DataVo (available on both `DbContext` and `DatabaseFacade`).
- **`LoadFromDataVo()`** synchronizes EF's change tracker from DataVo when rows were written by another context or directly through `DataVoContext`.
- **`ExplainQueryFromDataVo<T>(...)`** inspects whether a LINQ expression fits the supported DataVo-native translation subset before running it.

## Vector Query Preview Shims

Inside `QueryFromDataVo`, `DataVoVectorDbFunctions` exposes preview shims (`CosineDistance` and `L2Distance`) that translate to DataVo's `<=>` and `<->` SQL vector operators:

```csharp
float[] queryVector = [1f, 0f, 0f];

List<Document> nearest = ctx.QueryFromDataVo<Document>(q => q
    .Where(d => DataVoVectorDbFunctions.CosineDistance(EF.Functions, d.Embedding, queryVector) < 0.3)
    .OrderBy(d => DataVoVectorDbFunctions.CosineDistance(EF.Functions, d.Embedding, queryVector))
    .Take(5));
```

Note that `COSINE_DISTANCE()` and `L2_DISTANCE()` exist only as EF Core preview shims, not as core DataVo SQL scalar functions.

## Current Limitations

| Area | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `DbSet` CRUD (`Add`, `SaveChanges`, `LoadFromDataVo`) | Supported for mapped scalar CLR properties |
| `QueryFromDataVo` / `QueryFromDataVoAsync` | Supported for bounded `Where`, `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`, `Skip`, `Take`, `Select` |
| Vector distance shims (`CosineDistance`, `L2Distance`) | Preview translation inside `QueryFromDataVo` |
| EF Migrations (`dotnet ef migrations`), shadow properties, complex joins, `GroupBy` | **Not supported** (unsupported patterns throw `DataVoEfException`) |
| Native AOT (`PublishAot=true`) | **Not supported** |

## See Also

- [Compiled LINQ & Spatial Queries](/manual/client-interfaces/compiled-linq): AOT-safe, zero-reflection LINQ alternative
- [Error Handling](/manual/reference/error-handling): `DataVoEfException` and engine error codes
- [Native AOT Deployment](/manual/client-interfaces/native-aot): Why `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` is excluded from AOT

# SQL Compatibility

> Source route: /manual/sql/compatibility
> Source file: manual/sql/compatibility.md

DataVo SQL is a compact embedded-engine dialect designed for predictable, zero-allocation execution in .NET. It covers standard relational CRUD, joins, aggregates, transactions, and vector search without emulating PostgreSQL or SQLite system catalogs.

```sql
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    category VARCHAR(80),
    embedding VECTOR(384)
);

SELECT id, title, embedding <=> '[0.1, 0.2, ...]' AS distance
FROM documents
WHERE category = 'guide'
ORDER BY distance ASC
LIMIT 5;
```

## Dialect Matrix (DataVo v0.4 vs. SQLite & PostgreSQL)

| Feature | DataVo v0.4 | SQLite / PostgreSQL Difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CREATE` / `DROP` (`DATABASE`, `TABLE`, `INDEX`) | Supported | Uses `DROP INDEX name ON table`; supports `USING BTREE`, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, `COLUMNAR`. |
| `ALTER TABLE` | Limited | Supports `ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, `MODIFY COLUMN`; rejects key, FK, or indexed column changes. |
| `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `VACUUM` | Supported | No `MERGE`, `UPSERT` (`ON CONFLICT`), `RETURNING`, or PostgreSQL `COPY`. |
| Transactions & Savepoints | Supported | Snapshot isolation via `BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, `SAVEPOINT`, `ROLLBACK TO`, `RELEASE`; not serializable. |
| `SELECT`, `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`, `OFFSET` | Supported | `SELECT DISTINCT` runs on the general evaluator; `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k` uses bounded top-k on typed paths. |
| Joins (`INNER`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `FULL`, `CROSS`) | Supported | `INNER`/`LEFT` on integer keys use typed hash joins; `RIGHT`/`FULL`/`CROSS` and text/`GUID` keys use the general path. |
| Aggregates, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING` | Supported | `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX` (including `DISTINCT`); `HAVING` works with or without `GROUP BY`. |
| Subqueries & CTEs | Supported | `IN (SELECT ...)`, `EXISTS`, `NOT EXISTS`; non-recursive `WITH` CTEs (`WITH RECURSIVE` is reactive-only). |
| Set Operations | Partial | `UNION` and `UNION ALL` supported; `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` are not supported. |
| Window Functions | Limited | `RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...)` only; no `ROW_NUMBER`, `DENSE_RANK`, `LAG`, `LEAD`, or frames. |
| Scalar Functions & Expressions | Limited | `LOWER`, `UPPER`, arithmetic `+ - * /`; no `CASE WHEN`, `COALESCE`, `CAST`, `PRAGMA`, or date/math functions. |
| Vector Search (`VECTOR(n)`, `<->`, `<=>`) | Supported | Native DataVo extension (similar to `pgvector`, without `<#>` inner-product). |
| Views, Triggers, Procedures, UDFs | Not supported | Use [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) (`Subscribe`) for continuous queries in C#. |
| System Catalogs (`pg_class`, `sqlite_master`) | Not supported | Use `SHOW DATABASES`, `SHOW TABLES`, `DESCRIBE <table>`, and `EXPLAIN`. |
| RBAC Security Commands | Supported | `CREATE USER`/`ROLE`, `GRANT`, `REVOKE`, `LOGIN`, `LOGOUT`, `SHOW USERS`/`ROLES`/`GRANTS` (not PostgreSQL roles). |

## Execution Paths & Performance Notes

Every construct marked **Supported** returns identical results across storage modes, but execution speed varies by path:

- **Typed fast paths:** Single-table filters, aggregates, `BETWEEN` on clustered primary keys, and `INNER`/`LEFT` joins on integer equality keys read stored rows directly with minimal allocations.
- **General evaluator:** `SELECT DISTINCT`, `RIGHT`/`FULL`/`CROSS` joins, joins on `VARCHAR` or `GUID` keys, cross-table `OR` predicates, CTEs, window functions, and queries inside explicit transactions materialize row dictionaries and are slower on large tables.

## Key Type Differences

- **`FLOAT` is 32-bit** (`System.Single`), unlike SQLite `REAL` or SQL Server `FLOAT` (64-bit). Use `DOUBLE` for 64-bit floating-point values.
- **`VARCHAR` comparisons are ordinal** (UTF-8 byte/code-point order), not collation-aware or case-insensitive.
- **No silent type fallbacks:** Unsupported types such as `DECIMAL`, `NUMERIC`, and `TIME` throw an explicit `ParserException` instead of silently storing text.

## See Also
- [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types): Supported SQL types, .NET CLR mappings, and unsupported type errors
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner): How DataVo chooses between typed fast paths and the general evaluator
- [Functions & Operators](/manual/sql/functions): Complete list of aggregates, window functions, scalar functions, and operators

---

# Data Types

> Source route: /manual/sql/data-types
> Source file: manual/sql/data-types.md

Every column in a DataVo table has a strict schema type. DataVo stores each accepted type natively and rejects unsupported SQL types with an explicit `ParserException` rather than silently falling back to text.

```sql
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    external_id GUID,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    published_on DATE,
    rating DOUBLE,
    is_public BIT,
    embedding VECTOR(384)
);
```

## Supported SQL Types

| Canonical Type | Accepted Aliases | .NET CLR Type | Storage & Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INT` | `INTEGER`, `SMALLINT`, `TINYINT`, `MEDIUMINT` | `int` (`Int32`) | 32-bit signed integer. Single `INT` primary key is clustered on `Lsm`. |
| `BIGINT` | — | `long` (`Int64`) | 64-bit signed integer. Also used as the return type of `COUNT(...)`. |
| `FLOAT` | `REAL` | `float` (`Single`) | 32-bit IEEE 754 float (not 64-bit like SQLite `REAL`). |
| `DOUBLE` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | `double` (`Double`) | 64-bit IEEE 754 double. |
| `BIT` | `BOOL`, `BOOLEAN` | `bool` (`Boolean`) | Accepts `TRUE`/`FALSE` (any case); `1`/`0` and `'true'`/`'false'` are also parsed. |
| `DATE` | — | `DataVoDate` | Calendar date stored as a 32-bit day count since `0001-01-01`. |
| `DATETIME` | `TIMESTAMP`, `DATETIME2`, `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `DateTime` (UTC), `DateTimeOffset` | A point in time stored as 8-byte UTC ticks (100 ns precision, `0001-01-01` to `9999-12-31`). |
| `GUID` | `UUID`, `UNIQUEIDENTIFIER` | `Guid` | 128-bit UUID. Single `GUID` primary key is clustered on `Lsm`. |
| `VARCHAR(n)` | `NVARCHAR`, `CHAR`, `NCHAR`, `TEXT`, `STRING` | `string` | UTF-8 variable-length text. Comparisons and sorting are ordinal (case-sensitive). |
| `VECTOR(n)` | `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, `REAL[n]` | `float[]`, `ReadOnlyMemory<float>` | Fixed-dimension `n`-element array of 32-bit floats. `[DataVoTable]` models declare it with `[VectorDimensions(n)]`. |

::: info DataVo Extension
`VECTOR(n)` (with `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, and `REAL[n]` shorthands) and `GUID` (`UUID`, `UNIQUEIDENTIFIER`) are first-class DataVo extensions beyond standard SQLite. `VECTOR` is a reserved keyword, so a column cannot be named `Vector`.
:::

## The `DATE` Storage & Row Contract

`DATE` stores only a calendar date (with no time-of-day or timezone component) as a zero-based 32-bit `DayNumber` (`0` = `0001-01-01`, `3652058` = `9999-12-31`).

- **Query materialization:** Reading a `DATE` column returns a `DataVoDate` struct (`DataVo.Core.DataVoDate`).
- **.NET interoperability:** On `.NET 10`, convert cleanly with `DataVoDate.FromDateOnly(DateOnly)` / `.ToDateOnly()` or `DataVoDate.FromDateTime(DateTime)` / `.ToDateTime()` (midnight `DateTimeKind.Unspecified`).
- **Timestamps:** For a point in time with sub-day precision, use `DATETIME` (below).

## The `DATETIME` / `TIMESTAMP` Storage & Row Contract

`DATETIME` (aliases `TIMESTAMP`, `DATETIME2`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`) stores an instant as the `Ticks` of its UTC time: an 8-byte `long`. Packed rows, B-Tree keys, clustered keys and SIMD columnar scans (including LSM zone maps) compare it as a plain 64-bit integer, with no per-row conversion.

- **Writing:** a `DateTime` of kind `Local` is converted to UTC; kinds `Utc` and `Unspecified` are taken as UTC as they are. A `DateTimeOffset` keeps its instant (`UtcTicks`). SQL literals are ISO 8601 in the invariant culture: `'2026-11-24'`, `'2026-11-24 10:15:00'`, `'2026-11-24T10:15:00.1234567Z'`, `'2026-11-24T12:15:00+02:00'`. Text without an offset is UTC.
- **Reading:** SQL results return `DateTime` with `Kind = Utc`. Generated tables map `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` (returned at offset zero) and their nullable forms; compiled readers have `GetDateTime`, `GetDateTimeOffset` and their `...OrNull` forms.
- **Parameters:** `DataVoQueryParameter` accepts `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset`. A `DATE` column given a `DateTime` keeps its date as given.
- **Indexes:** secondary indexes key a `DATETIME` on its fixed-width canonical UTC text (`yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffffffZ`), so any spelling of the same instant finds the row through the index.
- **Aggregates:** `MIN`, `MAX` and `COUNT` work everywhere, including `USING COLUMNAR` indexes. `SUM`/`AVG` of instants are not computed by the columnar kernels.

```sql
CREATE TABLE events (id INT PRIMARY KEY, at DATETIME, label VARCHAR(40));
INSERT INTO events VALUES (1, '2026-11-24T12:15:00+02:00', 'deploy');
SELECT id FROM events WHERE at >= '2026-11-24 10:00:00' ORDER BY at DESC;
```

## Unsupported Types (`ParserException`)

DataVo throws a `ParserException` at `CREATE TABLE` or `ALTER TABLE` time for types it cannot store faithfully:

| Unsupported Type | Error Guidance / Workaround |
| --- | --- |
| `DECIMAL`, `NUMERIC`, `MONEY` | Use `DOUBLE` for approximate numeric values, or `VARCHAR` to preserve exact decimal digits. |
| `TIME` | Use `DATETIME` (or `TIMESTAMP`) for a point in time, or `DATE` for a calendar date. |
| `LONG` | Use `BIGINT` for 64-bit integers. |
| `BLOB`, `BINARY`, `VARBINARY`, `JSON`, `JSONB` | Not supported as native column types in `v0.4`; encode as `VARCHAR` (e.g., Base64 or JSON text). |

## See Also
- [CREATE TABLE](/manual/sql/statements/create-table): Declaring columns, constraints, and defaults in `CREATE TABLE`
- [Indexes](/manual/sql/statements/indexes): Choosing B-Tree, HNSW, FLAT, or COLUMNAR indexes by column type
- [SQL Compatibility](/manual/sql/compatibility): Full dialect comparison against SQLite and PostgreSQL

---

# SELECT

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/select
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/select.md

The `SELECT` statement queries one or more tables or common table expressions (CTEs), applies row filters, joins, grouping, window ranking, ordering, and pagination, and returns a result set.

## Syntax

```sql
[WITH cte_name AS (select_statement) [, ...]]
SELECT [DISTINCT]
    { * | table_or_alias.* | expression [[AS] alias] } [, ...]
FROM table_name [[AS] alias]
    [{ [INNER] | LEFT [OUTER] | RIGHT [OUTER] | FULL [OUTER] | CROSS }
     JOIN table_name [[AS] alias] [ON join_condition]] [...]
[WHERE filter_condition]
[GROUP BY column_ref [, ...]]
[HAVING group_condition]
[UNION [ALL] select_statement [...]]
[ORDER BY expression [ASC | DESC] [, ...]]
[LIMIT count [OFFSET skip]]
```

## Parameters

| Clause / Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `WITH cte_name AS (...)` | Defines one or more non-recursive common table expressions scoped to the query. |
| `DISTINCT` | Eliminates duplicate output rows after projection. |
| `expression [[AS] alias]` | Column reference, literal, arithmetic expression, aggregate, `RANK()` window expression, scalar function (`LOWER`, `UPPER`), or vector distance (`<->`, `<=>`). |
| `FROM table_name [[AS] alias]` | Source base table or CTE name, with an optional alias. |
| `JOIN ... ON join_condition` | Combines rows from multiple tables using `INNER`, `LEFT [OUTER]`, `RIGHT [OUTER]`, `FULL [OUTER]`, or `CROSS JOIN`. |
| `WHERE filter_condition` | Filters individual rows before grouping and projection. |
| `GROUP BY column_ref, ...` | Partitions matching rows into groups for aggregate evaluation. |
| `HAVING group_condition` | Filters aggregated groups; also supported without `GROUP BY` to filter a single whole-table aggregate group. |
| `UNION [ALL]` | Vertically combines the result rows of two or more compatible `SELECT` queries. |
| `ORDER BY expression [ASC \| DESC]` | Sorts result rows ascending (`ASC`, default) or descending (`DESC`). |
| `LIMIT count [OFFSET skip]` | Caps the number of returned rows and optionally skips the first `skip` rows. |

## Columns & Aliases

Project all columns with `*`, qualify columns by table or alias (`p.Name`), or compute derived values with arithmetic, scalar functions, aggregates, and vector distances. Use `AS` (optional) to assign an output column name.

```sql
SELECT
    p.Id,
    UPPER(p.Name) AS PlayerName,
    p.Score + 100 AS BoostedScore,
    p.Region
FROM players AS p;
```

- Column aliases are reflected in result headers and can be referenced in `ORDER BY`.
- When joining multiple tables that share column names (such as `Id`), qualify each reference with its table name or alias to avoid ambiguity errors.

## FROM

The `FROM` clause specifies the primary table or CTE to read. Assigning a short alias makes multi-table queries and qualified column references concise.

```sql
SELECT p.Name, p.Score
FROM players p;
```

## WHERE

The `WHERE` clause filters rows before grouping or window evaluation. DataVo supports comparison, logical, pattern, range, nullability, subquery, and vector distance predicates.

```sql
SELECT Id, Name, Score, Region
FROM players
WHERE Region IN ('EU', 'NA')
  AND Score BETWEEN 500 AND 1500
  AND Name LIKE 'A%'
  AND Name NOT LIKE '%_bot'
  AND Region IS NOT NULL;
```

Supported `WHERE` predicates include:

- **Comparison:** `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` (text comparisons are ordinal UTF-8 code-point order).
- **Logical:** `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (with parentheses for grouping).
- **Membership & Range:** `IN (v1, v2, ...)`, `NOT IN (...)`, `BETWEEN low AND high`, `NOT BETWEEN low AND high`.
- **Pattern & Null:** `LIKE`, `NOT LIKE` (`%` matches any sequence, `_` matches any single character), `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`.
- **Vector Distance:** `<->` (L2 / Euclidean) and `<=>` (Cosine) against a `VECTOR(n)` column.

::: info DataVo Extension
Vector distance operators `<->` (L2) and `<=>` (Cosine) can be used directly inside `WHERE` predicates to filter by a maximum distance threshold:

```sql
SELECT Id, Title, Category
FROM documents
WHERE Category = 'guide'
  AND Embedding <=> '[0.12, 0.85, 0.44]' < 0.25;
```

Vector literals must be single-quoted strings (or bound parameters such as `@queryVec`) whose element count matches the column's declared `VECTOR(n)` dimension.
:::

::: tip Clustered Range Seeks
`BETWEEN` and range predicates on a clustered primary key (single `INT` or `GUID` `PRIMARY KEY` in `Lsm` mode) perform an index range seek instead of a full table scan.
:::

## JOIN

DataVo supports `INNER JOIN`, `LEFT [OUTER] JOIN`, `RIGHT [OUTER] JOIN`, `FULL [OUTER] JOIN`, `CROSS JOIN`, self-joins, and multi-table join chains.

### INNER and LEFT JOIN

```sql
SELECT
    p.Name,
    p.Region,
    m.Points,
    m.PlayedOn
FROM players p
INNER JOIN matches m ON m.PlayerId = p.Id
WHERE m.Points >= 50;
```

Use `LEFT JOIN` (or `LEFT OUTER JOIN`) to retain rows from the left table even when no matching row exists on the right (`NULL` fills unmatched right columns):

```sql
SELECT
    p.Id,
    p.Name,
    m.Points
FROM players p
LEFT JOIN matches m ON m.PlayerId = p.Id;
```

### RIGHT, FULL OUTER, and CROSS JOIN

```sql
-- Retain all match rows even if a player record is missing
SELECT p.Name, m.Id AS MatchId, m.Points
FROM players p
RIGHT OUTER JOIN matches m ON m.PlayerId = p.Id;

-- Retain unmatched rows from both sides
SELECT p.Name, m.Id AS MatchId
FROM players p
FULL OUTER JOIN matches m ON m.PlayerId = p.Id;

-- Cartesian product (no ON clause)
SELECT p.Name, d.Title
FROM players p
CROSS JOIN documents d;
```

::: tip Join Fast Paths
`INNER JOIN` and `LEFT JOIN` on integer equality keys execute on DataVo's typed hash-join path across any number of joined tables. `RIGHT JOIN`, `FULL OUTER JOIN`, `CROSS JOIN`, self-joins, `VARCHAR`/`GUID` join keys, and cross-table `OR` predicates are fully supported via the general evaluator.
:::

## GROUP BY & HAVING

`GROUP BY` partitions rows sharing identical values across one or more columns so aggregate functions (`COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`) compute one result per group. `HAVING` filters the resulting groups.

```sql
SELECT
    p.Region,
    COUNT(*) AS PlayerCount,
    AVG(p.Score) AS AvgScore,
    MAX(p.Score) AS TopScore
FROM players p
WHERE p.Score > 0
GROUP BY p.Region
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 AND AVG(p.Score) >= 600
ORDER BY AvgScore DESC;
```

- `HAVING` can reference aggregates that are not projected in the `SELECT` list.
- `HAVING` is also valid **without** `GROUP BY`; in that case, the filtered table is treated as a single group:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS ActivePlayers, SUM(Score) AS TotalScore
FROM players
WHERE Score >= 100
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0;
```

## DISTINCT

Add `DISTINCT` immediately after `SELECT` to deduplicate identical output rows.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT Region
FROM players
ORDER BY Region ASC;
```

For per-aggregate deduplication rather than whole-row deduplication, pass `DISTINCT` inside an aggregate call (for example, `COUNT(DISTINCT Region)`). See [Functions & Operators](/manual/sql/functions) for details.

## ORDER BY

`ORDER BY` sorts the final result set by one or more columns, aliases, or expressions. Each sort key accepts `ASC` (default) or `DESC`.

```sql
SELECT Id, Name, Region, Score
FROM players
ORDER BY Region ASC, Score DESC, Name ASC;
```

### Vector Distance Ranking

Combine `ORDER BY` with `<->` (L2) or `<=>` (Cosine) and `LIMIT` to run k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) similarity search:

```sql
SELECT
    Id,
    Title,
    Embedding <=> '[0.12, 0.85, 0.44]' AS Distance
FROM documents
WHERE Category = 'reference'
ORDER BY Distance ASC
LIMIT 5;
```

When an `HNSW` or `FLAT` index exists on `Embedding` with a matching distance metric, the planner accelerates `ORDER BY Embedding <=> ... LIMIT k` automatically.

## LIMIT & OFFSET

`LIMIT` restricts how many rows are returned. Combine `LIMIT` with `OFFSET` to paginate through sorted results.

```sql
-- Page 2 (rows 11 through 20)
SELECT Id, Name, Score
FROM players
ORDER BY Score DESC
LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10;
```

::: tip Top-K Execution
Queries of the form `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k` on typed scans and typed joins use a bounded top-k heap rather than sorting the entire table in memory.
:::

## Subqueries

DataVo supports `IN`, `EXISTS`, and `NOT EXISTS` subqueries inside `WHERE` predicates.

### `IN (SELECT ...)`

```sql
SELECT Id, Name, Score
FROM players
WHERE Id IN (
    SELECT PlayerId
    FROM matches
    WHERE Points >= 100
);
```

### `EXISTS` and `NOT EXISTS`

```sql
-- Players who have played at least one match
SELECT p.Id, p.Name
FROM players p
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM matches m
    WHERE m.PlayerId = p.Id
);

-- Players with no recorded matches
SELECT p.Id, p.Name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM matches m
    WHERE m.PlayerId = p.Id
);
```

## CTEs (`WITH`)

Use `WITH` to define one or more named temporary result sets (Common Table Expressions) that simplify complex queries. Non-recursive CTEs are materialized once before the outer `SELECT` executes and can be joined or aggregated like base tables.

```sql
WITH HighScorers AS (
    SELECT Id, Name, Region, Score
    FROM players
    WHERE Score >= 900
),
MatchTotals AS (
    SELECT PlayerId, SUM(Points) AS TotalPoints
    FROM matches
    GROUP BY PlayerId
)
SELECT
    h.Name,
    h.Region,
    m.TotalPoints
FROM HighScorers h
LEFT JOIN MatchTotals m ON m.PlayerId = h.Id
ORDER BY h.Score DESC;
```

::: info DataVo Extension: `WITH RECURSIVE`
Standard one-shot `SELECT` queries support non-recursive `WITH` CTEs. **`WITH RECURSIVE`** is supported specifically for [Live Reactive Views](/manual/fundamentals/reactive-views) created via `Subscribe` in C#.
:::

## Window Functions

DataVo v0.4 supports the `RANK()` window function to assign competition ranks (`1, 2, 2, 4, ...`) within optional partitions without collapsing rows.

```sql
SELECT
    Name,
    Region,
    Score,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Region ORDER BY Score DESC) AS RegionRank
FROM players
ORDER BY Region ASC, RegionRank ASC;
```

- `ORDER BY <column> [ASC | DESC]` inside `OVER (...)` is **required** and accepts a single column reference.
- `PARTITION BY <col1> [, <col2>, ...]` is **optional**; omitting it ranks across the entire result set.

::: warning Window Function Scope in v0.4
Only `RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY <col> [ASC | DESC])` is supported in v0.4. `ROW_NUMBER()`, `DENSE_RANK()`, `LAG()`, `LEAD()`, `FIRST_VALUE()`, `LAST_VALUE()`, and window frame clauses (`ROWS BETWEEN ...`) are not implemented and throw a `ParserException`.
:::

## Set Operations

Combine rows from two or more `SELECT` statements with matching column counts using `UNION` or `UNION ALL`.

```sql
-- Deduplicated union
SELECT Id, Name FROM players WHERE Region = 'EU'
UNION
SELECT Id, Name FROM players WHERE Score >= 1200;

-- Preserve all rows including duplicates
SELECT Id, Name FROM players WHERE Region = 'EU'
UNION ALL
SELECT Id, Name FROM players WHERE Region = 'NA';
```

- `UNION` removes duplicate rows across branches.
- `UNION ALL` concatenates all branch rows without deduplication and avoids the hashing cost.

::: warning Unsupported Set Operations
`INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT`, and parenthesized `UNION` sub-branches are not supported in v0.4.
:::

## See Also

- [Functions & Operators](/manual/sql/functions): Aggregates, `RANK()`, `LOWER`/`UPPER`, and vector distance operators
- [EXPLAIN](/manual/sql/statements/explain): Inspecting query plans, physical operators, and fast-path choices
- [Indexes](/manual/sql/statements/indexes): Accelerating `WHERE`, `JOIN`, and vector `ORDER BY` queries
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner): Typed fast paths, bounded top-k heaps, and general evaluator fallback rules

---

# INSERT

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/insert
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/insert.md

The `INSERT` statement adds one or more new rows into a table, validating all schema constraints (`PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `NOT NULL`, and `FOREIGN KEY`) and updating all table indexes atomically.

## Syntax

```sql
INSERT INTO table_name [(column1, column2, ...)]
VALUES (value1, value2, ...) [, (value1, value2, ...), ...];
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `table_name` | Target table to receive the new rows. |
| `(column1, column2, ...)` | Optional explicit list of target columns. Recommended for schema resilience; omitted columns receive their declared `DEFAULT` or `NULL`. |
| `VALUES (...) [, ...]` | One or more parenthesized tuples of literal values or bound parameters (`@param`). Each tuple must match the column count. |

## Single-Row Insert

Provide an explicit column list (recommended) or omit it for a positional full-row insert whose values match the table's declared column order.

```sql
-- Column-targeted insert (recommended)
INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region)
VALUES (1, 'Ada', 980, 'EU');

-- Positional full-row insert (must match column order in CREATE TABLE)
INSERT INTO players
VALUES (2, 'Grace', 1120, 'NA');
```

## Explicit Column Lists & Defaults

When you specify an explicit column list, any omitted column automatically receives its declared `DEFAULT` literal, or `NULL` if no default is defined and the column is nullable. Omitting a `NOT NULL` column without a default fails validation.

```sql
-- Region receives its DEFAULT value or NULL
INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score)
VALUES (3, 'Linus', 875);

-- Inserting explicit NULL values
INSERT INTO players (Id, Name, Score, Region)
VALUES (4, 'Margaret', 1050, NULL);
```

## Multi-Row `VALUES`

Insert multiple rows in a single statement by separating value tuples with commas. Multi-row inserts reduce parse overhead and execute under a single write lock in auto-commit mode.

```sql
INSERT INTO matches (Id, PlayerId, Points, PlayedOn)
VALUES
    (101, 1, 85, '2026-03-14'),
    (102, 2, 92, '2026-03-15'),
    (103, 1, 110, '2026-03-16');
```

## Inserting `VECTOR` Columns

::: info DataVo Extension
`VECTOR(n)` columns accept **single-quoted** bracketed float-array literals (such as `'[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]'`) or bound parameters (`@embedding`). The element count must exactly match the column's declared dimension `n`.
:::

```sql
-- Quoted vector literal (shown with a 3-element shorthand; provide 384 floats for VECTOR(384))
INSERT INTO documents (Id, Title, Category, Embedding)
VALUES (1, 'Quickstart Guide', 'guide', '[0.12, 0.85, 0.44]');

-- Bound parameter in parameterized SQL (recommended for high-dimensional VECTOR(384) embeddings)
INSERT INTO documents (Id, Title, Category, Embedding)
VALUES (@id, @title, @category, @embedding);
```

::: warning Literal & Expression Rules in `VALUES`
- **Quoted vectors only:** Unquoted array syntax like `[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]` is **not** accepted by the SQL parser and raises a syntax error. Always quote vector literals (`'[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]'`) or pass a `float[]` parameter.
- **No expressions in `VALUES`:** Arithmetic or function expressions inside `VALUES` (for example `VALUES (1, 'Ada', 100 + 50, 'EU')` or `UPPER('eu')`) are **not** parsed. Supply plain literals (`'text'`, `42`, `3.14`, `TRUE`, `NULL`) or bound `@parameters`.
:::

## Constraints, Indexes & Transactions

- **Constraint enforcement:** Every row is checked against `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `NOT NULL`, and `FOREIGN KEY` constraints before storage is modified. If any row in a multi-row batch fails validation, the statement aborts with an error.
- **Index maintenance:** All B-Tree, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, and `COLUMNAR` indexes on the table are updated automatically.
- **Transactions:** Inside an explicit `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` block, inserted rows are buffered in `TransactionContext`, visible immediately to subsequent queries in the same transaction, and cleanly discarded on `ROLLBACK` or `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`.

::: warning Unsupported `INSERT` Clauses in v0.4
The following SQL extensions are **not** supported in DataVo v0.4:
- `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE / DO NOTHING` (upsert)
- `INSERT OR REPLACE` / `REPLACE INTO`
- `INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...`
- `RETURNING` clauses

To upsert rows in application code, check existence or handle the key conflict inside a transaction, then run `UPDATE` or `INSERT`.
:::

## See Also

- [UPDATE](/manual/sql/statements/update): Modifying existing rows with `SET` expressions
- [DELETE](/manual/sql/statements/delete): Removing rows and compacting storage with `VACUUM`
- [CREATE TABLE](/manual/sql/statements/create-table): Defining column types, `DEFAULT` values, and constraints
- [Transactions](/manual/sql/statements/transactions): Grouping writes with `BEGIN`, `SAVEPOINT`, `COMMIT`, and `ROLLBACK`

---

# UPDATE

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/update
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/update.md

The `UPDATE` statement modifies one or more column values on existing rows matching an optional `WHERE` predicate, re-validating constraints and keeping all table indexes synchronized.

## Syntax

```sql
UPDATE table_name
SET column1 = expression1 [, column2 = expression2, ...]
[WHERE filter_condition];
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `table_name` | Target table whose rows will be updated. |
| `SET column = expression` | One or more comma-separated assignments. Supports literals, `@param` parameters, column references, binary arithmetic/string `+ - * /`, and scalar subqueries. |
| `WHERE filter_condition` | Optional predicate selecting which rows to modify. When omitted, **every row** in the table is updated. |

## Single & Multi-Column Updates

Update a single column or assign multiple columns in one `SET` clause:

```sql
-- Update a single column on one row
UPDATE players
SET Score = 1050
WHERE Id = 1;

-- Update multiple columns at once
UPDATE players
SET Score = 1200,
    Region = 'US'
WHERE Id = 2;
```

To update a `VECTOR(n)` column, provide a single-quoted float-array literal or a bound parameter matching the column's dimension:

```sql
UPDATE documents
SET Category = 'tutorial',
    Embedding = @newEmbedding
WHERE Id = 1;
```

## Expressions & Subqueries in `SET`

`SET` assignments evaluate column references, literals, bound parameters, binary operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`), and scalar subqueries (`(SELECT ...)`).

```sql
-- Arithmetic update referencing the current row
UPDATE players
SET Score = Score + 50
WHERE Region = 'EU';

-- String concatenation using '+'
UPDATE players
SET Name = Name + ' (VIP)'
WHERE Score >= 1200;

-- Scalar subquery assignment
UPDATE players
SET Score = (SELECT MAX(Points) FROM matches WHERE PlayerId = 1)
WHERE Id = 1;
```

- **NULL propagation:** In binary arithmetic expressions (`Score + 10`), if either operand is `NULL`, the expression evaluates to `NULL`.
- **Unknown columns:** Referencing a column that does not exist in the target table fails immediately with an unknown-column binding error before any row is modified.

::: warning No Scalar Functions in `SET`
`UPDATE ... SET` does **not** evaluate scalar functions such as `LOWER(...)` or `UPPER(...)`. Compute string transformations in application code and bind the result as a literal or `@param` instead.

Additionally, `UPDATE ... FROM` joins and `RETURNING` clauses are not supported in DataVo v0.4.
:::

## Filtering & Full-Table Updates

`WHERE` accepts the same predicates as `SELECT`, including comparisons, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, `IN`, `BETWEEN`, `LIKE`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, and subqueries.

```sql
UPDATE matches
SET Points = Points + 10
WHERE PlayedOn BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-03-31'
  AND Points < 100;
```

::: warning Omitting `WHERE` Updates Every Row
If you omit the `WHERE` clause, DataVo applies the `SET` assignments to **all rows** in the table:

```sql
-- Resets Score to 0 for every player in the table
UPDATE players
SET Score = 0;
```
:::

## Index Maintenance & Transactions

- **Automatic index updates:** Every `UPDATE` automatically maintains all B-Tree, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, and `COLUMNAR` indexes on the table. Updating an indexed or `VECTOR(n)` column removes stale entries and indexes the new values atomically.
- **Constraint checks:** Updating a `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `NOT NULL`, or `FOREIGN KEY` column re-validates all constraints before the change takes effect.
- **MVCC & transaction buffering:** Inside an explicit `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` transaction, `UPDATE` reads through the transaction's snapshot and its own prior uncommitted writes, coalesces buffered updates in `TransactionContext`, and is completely reversible via `ROLLBACK` or `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`.

## See Also

- [INSERT](/manual/sql/statements/insert): Adding new rows to a table
- [DELETE](/manual/sql/statements/delete): Removing rows and compacting storage with `VACUUM`
- [SELECT](/manual/sql/statements/select): Querying updated rows and `WHERE` predicate syntax
- [Transactions](/manual/sql/statements/transactions): Atomic multi-statement updates with `BEGIN`, `SAVEPOINT`, `COMMIT`, and `ROLLBACK`

---

# DELETE

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/delete
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/delete.md

The `DELETE` statement removes rows matching an optional `WHERE` predicate from a table, enforcing foreign-key referential actions and updating all table indexes.

## Syntax

```sql
DELETE FROM table_name
[WHERE filter_condition];
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `table_name` | Target table from which rows will be removed. |
| `WHERE filter_condition` | Optional predicate selecting which rows to delete. When omitted, **all rows** in the table are deleted. |

## Filtered `DELETE`

Provide a `WHERE` clause to remove only rows matching your condition. `WHERE` supports comparisons, logical operators, `IN`, `BETWEEN`, `LIKE`/`NOT LIKE`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, subqueries, and vector distance predicates.

```sql
-- Delete a single row by primary key
DELETE FROM players
WHERE Id = 4;

-- Delete with compound predicates
DELETE FROM matches
WHERE PlayedOn < '2025-01-01'
  AND Points = 0;

-- Delete using a subquery
DELETE FROM players
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM matches m
    WHERE m.PlayerId = players.Id
);
```

## Full-Table `DELETE`

Omitting the `WHERE` clause removes every row in the table while preserving the table schema, constraints, and index definitions.

```sql
DELETE FROM matches;
```

::: warning Destructive Operation
DataVo v0.4 does not have a `TRUNCATE TABLE` statement; `DELETE FROM table_name;` removes every row and executes through normal constraint, index, and transaction paths. Wrap bulk deletes inside `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` if you need an undo boundary.
:::

## Foreign Keys & Index Maintenance

- **Referential actions:** Deleting a parent row checks all referencing child tables. `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes dependent child rows automatically; `ON DELETE RESTRICT` rejects the `DELETE` if any child row still references the target key.
- **Automatic index cleanup:** Removed rows are purged from all B-Tree, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, and `COLUMNAR` indexes on the table.
- **Unsupported clauses:** `DELETE ... USING` joins and `RETURNING` clauses are not supported in DataVo v0.4.

## Transactions & Rollback Behavior

Inside an explicit transaction (`BEGIN` ... `COMMIT`), `DELETE` does not immediately destroy committed rows on disk. Instead, deletes are buffered in `TransactionContext`:

- **Read-your-own-writes:** Subsequent `SELECT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` statements inside the same transaction immediately exclude the deleted rows.
- **Buffered inserts:** If a row was inserted earlier in the same uncommitted transaction, `DELETE` drops it from the transaction's insert buffer.
- **Full reversibility:** Executing `ROLLBACK` or `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` cleanly discards the buffered deletes so committed rows remain untouched.

```sql
BEGIN;

DELETE FROM players WHERE Region = 'Legacy';
SAVEPOINT after_cleanup;

DELETE FROM players WHERE Score < 200;

-- Undo only the second delete
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT after_cleanup;

COMMIT;
```

## Reclaiming Space with `VACUUM`

Deleted rows remain as tombstones until storage compacts them. `Lsm` compacts them during background merges; to rewrite one table immediately (for example after a large purge), run `VACUUM` on it:

```sql
VACUUM players;
```

`VACUUM table_name` performs three steps:

1. Scans the table and strips all tombstoned (soft-deleted) rows.
2. Rewrites the surviving rows with fresh, contiguous internal row IDs.
3. Drops and rebuilds all B-Tree indexes on the table against the new row IDs.

::: info When You Need `VACUUM`
`Lsm` compacts deleted keys automatically during background and flush merges. `VACUUM <table>` is for reclaiming space at once after a large one-time purge.
:::

## See Also

- [INSERT](/manual/sql/statements/insert): Adding new rows to a table
- [UPDATE](/manual/sql/statements/update): Modifying existing rows
- [CREATE TABLE](/manual/sql/statements/create-table): Configuring `ON DELETE CASCADE` and `ON DELETE RESTRICT` foreign keys
- [Transactions](/manual/sql/statements/transactions): Using `BEGIN`, `SAVEPOINT`, `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`, and `COMMIT`

---

# CREATE TABLE

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/create-table
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/create-table.md

`CREATE TABLE` defines a new table in the active database along with its columns, data types, default values, and integrity constraints. DataVo enforces `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `NOT NULL`, `DEFAULT`, and `FOREIGN KEY` constraints at write time.

## Syntax

```sql
CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <table_name> (
    <column_name> <data_type>
        [NOT NULL | NULL]
        [DEFAULT <literal>]
        [PRIMARY KEY]
        [UNIQUE]
        [REFERENCES <ref_table> (<ref_col>) [ON DELETE CASCADE | RESTRICT]],
    ...,
    [[CONSTRAINT <name>] PRIMARY KEY (<col1> [, <col2>, ...])],
    [[CONSTRAINT <name>] UNIQUE (<col>)],
    [[CONSTRAINT <name>] FOREIGN KEY (<col>) REFERENCES <ref_table> (<ref_col>) [ON DELETE CASCADE | RESTRICT]]
);
```

## Parameters

| Clause | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IF NOT EXISTS` | No | Succeeds as a no-op if `<table_name>` already exists in the active database instead of throwing an error. |
| `<table_name>` | Yes | Unique table identifier within the active database. |
| `<column_name>` | Yes | Column identifier. Must be unique within the table and cannot be a reserved keyword such as `VECTOR`. |
| `<data_type>` | Yes | Any supported DataVo SQL type (`INT`, `BIGINT`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, `BIT`, `DATE`, `GUID`, `VARCHAR(n)`, `VECTOR(n)`, and their aliases). See [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types). |
| `NOT NULL` / `NULL` | No | Controls whether `NULL` values are rejected on `INSERT` and `UPDATE`. Columns allow `NULL` by default unless `NOT NULL` or `PRIMARY KEY` is specified. |
| `DEFAULT <literal>` | No | Constant fallback value used when a column is omitted from `INSERT`. Must be a literal (`NULL`, number, quoted string, `true`, or `false`). |
| `PRIMARY KEY` | No | Uniquely identifies rows. May be declared on one column or as a composite table-level constraint. At most one `PRIMARY KEY` per table. |
| `UNIQUE` | No | Enforces uniqueness across non-`NULL` values on a single column. Multiple `NULL` values are permitted. |
| `REFERENCES <ref_table>(<ref_col>)` | No | Declares a foreign-key reference to `<ref_table>(<ref_col>)`, with optional `ON DELETE CASCADE` or `ON DELETE RESTRICT` (default). |
| `CONSTRAINT <name>` | No | Optional SQL-standard prefix accepted before table-level constraints. The constraint name is parsed for compatibility and is not persisted in the catalog. |

## Basic Table Creation

Use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in startup scripts so schema initialization is idempotent:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS App;
USE App;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS departments (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL UNIQUE
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS employees (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    external_id GUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    department_id INT REFERENCES departments(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    hired_on DATE,
    active BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);
```

## Primary Keys

Each table may declare at most one `PRIMARY KEY`, either inline on a single column or as a table-level constraint. Declaring both a column-level and a table-level `PRIMARY KEY` on the same table throws a `ParserException`.

- **Single-column `INT` or `GUID` primary keys** are clustered on the `Lsm` storage engine, enabling fast key seeks and range scans.
- **Composite primary keys** are declared at the table level:

```sql
CREATE TABLE project_members (
    project_id INT NOT NULL,
    employee_id INT NOT NULL,
    role VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'contributor',
    CONSTRAINT pk_project_members PRIMARY KEY (project_id, employee_id)
);
```

::: tip
For optimal read and range-scan performance on `Lsm`, prefer a single `INT` or `GUID` `PRIMARY KEY` whenever your data model has a natural or surrogate key.
:::

## Nullability and Defaults

Columns are nullable by default; you may write `NULL` explicitly for clarity or `NOT NULL` to reject `NULL` on writes. `DEFAULT` accepts only constant literals:

```sql
CREATE TABLE settings (
    key VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    value VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    retries INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
    ratio DOUBLE NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.5,
    enabled BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    label VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'default'
);
```

Expression defaults such as `DEFAULT NOW()` or `DEFAULT (1 + 1)` are rejected at parse/validation time.

## Unique Constraints

`UNIQUE` may be declared inline on a column or as a single-column table constraint. Multiple `NULL` values are allowed in a `UNIQUE` column because scalar indexes omit `NULL` keys.

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    email VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    handle VARCHAR(60),
    CONSTRAINT uq_users_handle UNIQUE (handle)
);
```

Declaring a multi-column `UNIQUE (col1, col2)` constraint throws a `ParserException` in `v0.4`.

## Foreign Keys

Foreign keys validate parent row existence on `INSERT` and `UPDATE` and enforce referential actions on parent `DELETE`:

- `ON DELETE RESTRICT` (default): Rejects deleting a parent row while any child row references it.
- `ON DELETE CASCADE`: Automatically deletes referencing child rows when a parent row is deleted.

Foreign keys can be declared inline or at the table level. Table-level `FOREIGN KEY (<col>)` must reference a column declared earlier in the `CREATE TABLE` column list.

```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT NOT NULL,
    total DOUBLE NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
    CONSTRAINT fk_orders_customer
        FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

## Vector Columns

::: info DataVo Extension
`VECTOR(n)` and its shorthands (`VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, `REAL[n]`) are first-class DataVo extensions for storing fixed-dimension 32-bit float embeddings and spatial coordinates. `VECTOR` is a reserved keyword and cannot be used as a column name.
:::

```sql
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    embedding VECTOR(384)
);

CREATE TABLE world_entities (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    position VEC3 NOT NULL,
    velocity FLOAT[3]
);
```

After creating the table, attach an `HNSW` or `FLAT` index with [`CREATE INDEX`](/manual/sql/statements/indexes) to accelerate similarity search.

## Unsupported Constraints in v0.4

::: warning
`CHECK` constraints are **not supported** in DataVo `v0.4` and will fail with a `ParserException`. Enforce domain checks in application logic before writing.

Multi-column `UNIQUE (c1, c2)` constraints, expression-based `DEFAULT` clauses, and `ON UPDATE` foreign-key actions are also not supported in `v0.4`.
:::

## See Also

- [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types): Column types, aliases, and `.NET` CLR mappings
- [ALTER TABLE & DROP](/manual/sql/statements/alter-and-drop): Adding, modifying, and dropping columns or tables
- [CREATE INDEX](/manual/sql/statements/indexes): Creating `BTREE`, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, and `COLUMNAR` indexes
- [INSERT](/manual/sql/statements/insert): Populating tables and triggering constraint checks

---

# ALTER TABLE & DROP

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/alter-and-drop
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/alter-and-drop.md

Use `ALTER TABLE` to add, remove, or modify non-key columns on an existing table, and use `DROP TABLE` or `DROP INDEX` to remove schema objects from the active database.

## Syntax

```sql
-- Add a column
ALTER TABLE <table_name> ADD [COLUMN] <column_name> <data_type>
    [DEFAULT <literal>] [NOT NULL | NULL];

-- Drop a column
ALTER TABLE <table_name> DROP [COLUMN] <column_name>;

-- Modify a column
ALTER TABLE <table_name> MODIFY [COLUMN] <column_name> <data_type>
    [DEFAULT <literal>] [NOT NULL | NULL];

-- Drop a table
DROP TABLE [IF EXISTS] <table_name>;

-- Drop an index
DROP INDEX <index_name> ON <table_name>;
```

## Parameters

| Clause | Statement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ADD [COLUMN]` | `ALTER TABLE` | Appends a new column to `<table_name>` and backfills existing rows with its `DEFAULT` literal or `NULL`. The `COLUMN` keyword is optional. |
| `DROP [COLUMN]` | `ALTER TABLE` | Removes `<column_name>` from `<table_name>` and rewrites stored rows. The `COLUMN` keyword is optional. |
| `MODIFY [COLUMN]` | `ALTER TABLE` | Changes `<column_name>`'s data type, `VARCHAR(n)` length, nullability, or `DEFAULT` value, converting existing rows in place. The `COLUMN` keyword is optional. |
| `IF EXISTS` | `DROP TABLE` | Succeeds as a no-op if `<table_name>` does not exist. Supported on `DROP TABLE` and `DROP DATABASE`, **not** on `DROP INDEX`. |
| `ON <table_name>` | `DROP INDEX` | Required target table qualifier identifying which table owns `<index_name>`. |

::: warning Unsupported ALTER TABLE Operations
`RENAME COLUMN` and `RENAME TO` are **not yet supported** in DataVo `v0.4` and throw a `ParserException` (`Unknown ALTER TABLE operation`). To rename a table or column, create the new table or column, copy data over, and drop the old one.
:::

## `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`

`ADD COLUMN` acquires a table write lock, appends the column to the catalog, backfills all existing rows with the column's `DEFAULT` literal (or `NULL` if omitted), and rewrites the table and its existing indexes.

```sql
ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN title VARCHAR(80) DEFAULT 'engineer';
ALTER TABLE employees ADD bio VARCHAR(500) NULL;
ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN active BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT true;
```

### Restrictions

- **No key or FK constraints:** Adding a column with `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, or `REFERENCES` fails at execution time with a `CatalogException`.
- **`NOT NULL` on non-empty tables:** Adding a `NOT NULL` column without a `DEFAULT` literal on a table that already contains rows throws a `ConstraintViolationException` (`NotNullViolation`). Supply a `DEFAULT` literal so existing rows can be backfilled safely.

## `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN`

`DROP COLUMN` removes a column from the catalog, strips it from all existing rows, and rebuilds remaining table indexes.

```sql
ALTER TABLE employees DROP COLUMN bio;
ALTER TABLE employees DROP title;
```

### Restrictions

DataVo rejects `DROP COLUMN` with a `CatalogException` if the target column is:

- The last remaining column in the table.
- Part of the table's `PRIMARY KEY`.
- Declared `UNIQUE`.
- A `FOREIGN KEY` column.
- Referenced by another table's `FOREIGN KEY` (parent column).
- Part of any index (`BTREE`, `HNSW`, `FLAT`, or `COLUMNAR`). Drop the index first with `DROP INDEX`, then drop the column.

## `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN`

`MODIFY COLUMN` updates a column's type, maximum `VARCHAR(n)` length, nullability, or `DEFAULT` literal. Existing row values are validated and converted before the table is rewritten; if any existing row fails validation, the schema remains unchanged.

```sql
-- Widen a VARCHAR column
ALTER TABLE employees MODIFY COLUMN name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL;

-- Change default and nullability
ALTER TABLE employees MODIFY active BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT false;

-- Widen INT to BIGINT
ALTER TABLE metrics MODIFY COLUMN count BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
```

### Restrictions

- **Existing data validation:**
  - Switching a column to `NOT NULL` fails with `ConstraintViolationException` (`NotNullViolation`) if any existing row contains `NULL`.
  - Shrinking `VARCHAR(n)` fails with `ConstraintViolationException` (`ValueTooLong`) if any existing string exceeds the new length `n`; DataVo never silently truncates data.
  - Incompatible type conversions for existing values fail and leave the table untouched.
- **Protected columns:** You cannot modify a column that is a `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `FOREIGN KEY`, referenced parent column, or part of any index.
- **No constraint additions:** You cannot add `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, or `FOREIGN KEY` constraints via `MODIFY COLUMN`.

::: tip
Because `ALTER TABLE` rewrites the table under a write lock, group schema design choices into `CREATE TABLE` when possible and drop secondary indexes before altering indexed columns.
:::

## `DROP TABLE`

`DROP TABLE` removes the table definition, all stored rows, and all indexes attached to that table from the active database.

```sql
DROP TABLE temp_imports;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS staging_events;
```

Use `IF EXISTS` in cleanup or migration scripts so dropping an already-absent table succeeds without error.

## `DROP INDEX`

`DROP INDEX` removes an index from the catalog and deletes its physical index structure (B-Tree, HNSW/FLAT vector index, or Columnar segment registration) while keeping the underlying table data intact.

```sql
DROP INDEX ix_players_score ON players;
DROP INDEX ix_documents_emb ON documents;
DROP INDEX cx_players_stats ON players;
```

::: warning `ON <table>` Required & No `IF EXISTS`
In DataVo `v0.4`, `DROP INDEX` **requires** the `ON <table_name>` clause and does **not** support `IF EXISTS`. Running `DROP INDEX ix_foo;` or `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_foo ON bar;` throws a `ParserException`.
:::

## See Also

- [CREATE TABLE](/manual/sql/statements/create-table): Declaring tables, primary keys, unique constraints, and foreign keys
- [CREATE INDEX](/manual/sql/statements/indexes): Creating B-Tree, HNSW, FLAT, and Columnar indexes
- [Data Types](/manual/sql/data-types): Supported column types and length rules

---

# CREATE INDEX

> Source route: /manual/sql/statements/indexes
> Source file: manual/sql/statements/indexes.md

`CREATE INDEX` builds a secondary index on an existing table in the active database and populates it immediately from current rows. DataVo supports four index methods: `BTREE` for scalar lookups and ranges, `HNSW` and `FLAT` for vector similarity search, and `COLUMNAR` for vectorized analytical aggregations.

## Syntax

```sql
CREATE INDEX <index_name> ON <table_name> (<column_name> [, <column_name>, ...])
    [USING BTREE | HNSW | FLAT | COLUMNAR]
    [WITH (<option_name> = <value> [, ...])];
```

::: info DataVo Extension
`USING HNSW`, `USING FLAT`, `USING COLUMNAR`, and the `WITH (...)` index-tuning clause are DataVo extensions beyond standard SQLite and ANSI SQL.
:::

## Parameters

| Clause | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<index_name>` | Yes | Unique index name for `<table_name>`. |
| `ON <table_name>` | Yes | Existing table in the active database to index. |
| `(<column_name>, ...)` | Yes | One or more target columns. `HNSW` and `FLAT` require exactly one `VECTOR(n)` column; `BTREE` and `COLUMNAR` accept one or more columns. |
| `USING <method>` | No | Index implementation: `BTREE` (default when omitted), `HNSW`, `FLAT`, or `COLUMNAR`. |
| `WITH (<opt> = <val>, ...)` | No | Key-value tuning options for vector indexes (`HNSW` and `FLAT`). Option names ignore case and underscores. |

::: warning Syntax Notes in v0.4
`CREATE INDEX` does **not** support `UNIQUE` or `IF NOT EXISTS` in DataVo `v0.4`. To enforce uniqueness on a column, declare `UNIQUE` inside [`CREATE TABLE`](/manual/sql/statements/create-table).
:::

## Index Methods Overview

| Method | Syntax | Target Columns | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BTREE` (default) | `USING BTREE` (or omit `USING`) | Single or composite scalar columns | Equality lookups, range scans, selective join probes, and single-key integer `GROUP BY COUNT`. |
| `HNSW` | `USING HNSW [WITH (...)]` | Single `VECTOR(n)` column | Fast approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search on medium and large embedding tables. |
| `FLAT` | `USING FLAT [WITH (metric = ...)]` | Single `VECTOR(n)` column | Exact exhaustive vector search on small tables and recall benchmarks. |
| `COLUMNAR` | `USING COLUMNAR` | Numeric (`INT`, `BIGINT`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`), `BIT`, and `DATE` columns | Vectorized `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, and `MAX` aggregations without decoding full rows. |

## Scalar B-Tree Indexes (`USING BTREE`)

B-Tree is the default index method when `USING` is omitted. You can index a single scalar column or a composite list of columns:

```sql
-- Single-column B-Tree index
CREATE INDEX ix_players_score ON players (score);

-- Explicit USING BTREE on a composite key
CREATE INDEX ix_players_region_score ON players (region, score) USING BTREE;
```

### Behavior & Query Acceleration

- **`NULL` keys:** A row whose key has a `NULL` in any indexed column never matches an equality or range lookup, so `IS NULL` predicates scan table rows and multiple `NULL`s may coexist in a `UNIQUE` column. `Lsm` indexes still record such rows under a dedicated `NULL` key (every `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `COMMIT` and rebuild path does this the same way), so a counting `GROUP BY` on an indexed integer column gets its `NULL` group from the index without reading the table. `InMemory` indexes hold no entry for them and count that group from the rows' null flags.
- **When B-Tree accelerates queries:**
  - Single-column equality predicates (`WHERE score = 500`) use an index point lookup.
  - Selective `INNER JOIN` probes on indexed integer keys probe the B-Tree instead of streaming the full table.
  - Whole-table `GROUP BY <indexed_int_col>` with `COUNT(*)` or `COUNT(col)` streams groups directly in key order from the index.
  - Secondary B-Tree indexes are **not** used to satisfy general `ORDER BY` clauses or non-counting `GROUP BY` shapes (see [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner)).

## Vector Indexes (`USING HNSW` & `USING FLAT`)

Vector indexes require **exactly one** `VECTOR(n)` column (`VECTOR(n)`, `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `FLOAT[n]`, or `REAL[n]`). Rows where the vector column is `NULL` are skipped.

```sql
-- Approximate HNSW index for text embeddings
CREATE INDEX ix_documents_emb ON documents (embedding)
USING HNSW WITH (
    metric = 'cosine',
    m = 16,
    ef_construction = 64,
    ef_search = 64,
    enable_diversity_heuristic = true
);

-- Exact FLAT index for 3D spatial coordinates
CREATE INDEX ix_entities_pos ON world_entities (position)
USING FLAT WITH (metric = 'euclidean');
```

### Vector `WITH (...)` Options

Passing HNSW graph options (`m`, `ef_construction`, `ef_search`, `enable_diversity_heuristic`) to `FLAT` or `BTREE`, passing `metric` to `BTREE`, or specifying out-of-range values throws a `BindingException` and creates no index. Option names ignore case and underscores (for example, `efConstruction` and `ef_construction` are equivalent).

| Option | Default | Valid Range | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metric` | `'cosine'` | `'cosine'`, `'euclidean'` (alias `'l2'`) | `HNSW`, `FLAT` | Distance metric persisted in the catalog. Use `'cosine'` for normalized embeddings and `'euclidean'`/`'l2'` for spatial positions. |
| `m` | `16` | `2` – `128` | `HNSW` | Maximum bi-directional links per graph layer (doubled on layer 0). Higher values improve recall at higher memory and build cost. |
| `ef_construction` | `64` | `1` – `4096` | `HNSW` | Candidate beam width during graph construction. Higher values yield better graph quality at slower build speed. |
| `ef_search` | `64` | `1` – `4096` | `HNSW` | Minimum candidate beam width during nearest-neighbor search. |
| `enable_diversity_heuristic` | `true` | `true`, `false` | `HNSW` | Preserves cross-cluster links during neighbor selection; disable only for faster builds on uniform data. |

### Filtered Vector Search Behavior

For hybrid queries combining `WHERE` predicates with `ORDER BY embedding <=> @q LIMIT k` (or `<->`), DataVo automatically widens the candidate beam and switches to an exact SIMD scan when graph traversal would cost more than scanning stored vectors, ensuring filtered `LIMIT k` queries return all `k` matching rows whenever enough rows qualify.

## Columnar Indexes (`USING COLUMNAR`)

Columnar indexes store selected columns in compact typed column chunks so analytical aggregates avoid reading full row payloads.

```sql
CREATE INDEX cx_players_stats ON players (score, id) USING COLUMNAR;
```

### Eligibility & Storage Rules

- **Allowed column types:** `INT`, `BIGINT`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, `BIT`, `DATE`, and `DATETIME` only (a `DATETIME` is kept as its UTC ticks and scanned with the 64-bit integer kernels; `MIN`/`MAX`/`COUNT` fold natively). Any other type (such as `VARCHAR`, `GUID`, or `VECTOR`) is rejected at `CREATE INDEX` time.
- **Storage modes:**
  - `InMemory`: Stores 4–8 bytes per row per indexed column in RAM for SIMD-accelerated scans.
  - `Lsm`: Persists format-v8 columnar segments inside `.sst` files with `min`/`max`/`NULL`/`NaN` zone maps for chunk skipping.
- **Query eligibility:** Accelerates `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, and `MAX` queries **without `GROUP BY`** whose `WHERE` clause is an `AND` of column-to-literal comparisons or `IS NULL` checks over indexed columns. Queries fall back cleanly to row scans when:
  - Running inside an explicit `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` transaction.
  - Using `GROUP BY`.
  - Filtering on comparisons where precision could differ (such as a fractional literal against an `INT` column), `BIT`/`DATE` predicates, or `NaN` floats.
  - Computing `SUM` or `AVG` over `FLOAT`/`DOUBLE` on an `Lsm` table with an unflushed memtable tail (to preserve deterministic floating-point addition order).
- **Consolidation & scope:** Columnar indexes never serve point lookups and do not replace B-Tree indexes. Multiple `USING COLUMNAR` indexes on the same table are consolidated internally.

::: tip Choosing the Right Index
- Use **`BTREE`** for selective `WHERE col = ...` filters and join keys.
- Use **`HNSW`** for `VECTOR(n)` tables with thousands or millions of rows; use **`FLAT`** for small tables or exact recall baselines.
- Use **`COLUMNAR`** for dashboard rollups (`COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`) over numeric columns.
:::

## Dropping an Index

Remove any index using [`DROP INDEX`](/manual/sql/statements/alter-and-drop#drop-index):

```sql
DROP INDEX ix_players_score ON players;
```

## See Also

- [ALTER TABLE & DROP](/manual/sql/statements/alter-and-drop): Dropping indexes (`DROP INDEX ... ON <table>`) and altering indexed columns
- [Vector Search](/manual/fundamentals/vector-search): Embeddings, `<=>` / `<->` distance operators, and hybrid vector queries
- [Query Planner](/manual/internals/query-planner): How DataVo routes queries to B-Tree, HNSW, FLAT, and Columnar fast paths
- [EXPLAIN](/manual/sql/statements/explain): Inspecting logical and physical execution plans
